Ownership and fairness

Each fixed outer player slot maps to a separate deterministic legacy player-1 game engine. No array index or image position grants membership. A spectator's contacts cannot hit another slot's targets. Targets and balls are personal rather than a shared race. Settings and initial seed match, but tracking pauses and adaptive placement can produce different wall-clock finish times. Scores are individual arcade results, not a certified competitive leaderboard.

Missing joints pause only the affected game. Compatible missing/tentative same-ID evidence can recover inside the proposed 450 ms source-and-receipt window. Both per-slot sessions and the shared source clock guard use that window; frame-loop expiry works without another packet. Recovery pauses engines before replacing input, so gesture history breaks even if missing and recovered packets arrive between display ticks. No stale coordinates are replayed. Explicit ambiguity, replacement, duplicate identity, expired recovery, camera restart or changed geometry requires explicit fresh admission. Scores remain attached to their old slot until Leave clears it.

The same integration fixes default single-player self-occlusion handling. SinglePlayerSession defaults remain unchanged. This PR is explicitly stacked on tracking PR #66 and must land after that dependency. Only additive exports touch its public entry. New modules are source-only and build through the mirror consumer. There is no new runtime dependency, acquisition path or collision algorithm.

Experimental software evidence only. No participant footage or training data was supplied. Physical identity continuity, height/clothing/occlusion variation, three-player throughput, camera alignment, movement comfort, external latency and collision accuracy remain unmeasured. No 99% continuity or three-player hardware certification is claimed. Multiplayer stays inline; the separate game window remains single-player.
